stories.headline: Qualcomm unveils Dragonfly C1000 data center CPU, signs Meta, buys Modular for $3.9B

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm announced its Dragonfly C1000 data center CPU and a strategic multi-generation agreement to supply Meta's next-generation server fleet, at its Investor Day 2026 in New York on June 24
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: QCOM) and Meta today announced a strategic multi-generation collaboration for Qualcomm Technologies to be a supplier for data center CPUs for Meta. Qualcomm Technologies' data center CPU, the Qualcomm Dragonfly C1000, is planned to power Meta's next-generation server fleet.

key_facts.fact: The Dragonfly C1000 will enter production in the second half of 2028; Qualcomm says it runs cores above 5 GHz and offers more than 250 cores
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm's first-generation Qualcomm Dragonfly C1000 CPU will be in production starting in the second half of 2028.

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm also unveiled the Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator, Qualcomm High Bandwidth Compute (HBC), and connectivity products, positioning itself as a full-stack data center supplier for the 'agentic AI era'
key_facts.excerpt: new data center solutions, including the Qualcomm Dragonfly C1000 CPU, Qualcomm High Bandwidth Compute (HBC), Qualcomm Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator, and connectivity products, together with custom silicon solutions

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm confirmed it will acquire AI-software startup Modular in an all-stock deal valued at more than $3.9 billion, to provide a 'silicon-agnostic compute layer' across CPU, GPU, NPU and custom ASICs
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm on Wednesday said that it will spend $3.9 billion to purchase AI-native software platform developer Modular Inc., a move that Qualcomm says will allow it to level the playing field on data centers by creating 'a silicon-agnostic compute layer.'

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm framed the data center push around a $200 billion target market; CEO Cristiano Amon called the Meta agreement 'a significant validation' of the company's performance-per-watt approach
key_facts.excerpt: All of this targeting a $200 billion market... These processors will run the industry fastest cores, running greater than 5 GHz. This is more than 30% faster than any of the competition. Coupled to that, we offer more than 250 cores.

key_facts.fact: Despite the announcements, Qualcomm shares fell about 5% on the session as investors weighed the cost of the Modular acquisition against data center revenue that won't arrive until H2 2028
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm shares are trading at $193.61, down 5.15% on the session, as investors weigh the near-term cost of a separate ~$4 billion acquisition against data center revenue that won't arrive until the second half of 2028.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil Jalapeño, a custom LLM inference chip taped out in nine months

key_facts.fact: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled Jalapeño on June 24, OpenAI's first custom AI accelerator, designed specifically for LLM inference rather than as a general-purpose GPU
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) today unveiled Jalapeño, OpenAI's first Intelligence Processor: an accelerator architected around OpenAI's vision for the future of LLM inference, and the first AI accelerator in a multi-generation compute platform the companies are building together.

key_facts.fact: The chip went from design to manufacturing tape-out in just nine months, which the companies call the fastest ASIC development cycle ever achieved in high-performance semiconductors, aided by OpenAI's own models
key_facts.excerpt: Jalapeño was co-developed from initial design to manufacturing tape-out in just nine months, and the custom AI accelerator program represents what we believe to be the fastest ASIC development cycle ever achieved in high-performance advanced semiconductors.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI plans to deploy Jalapeño by the end of 2026 as the first step in a multi-generation chip development plan; it is a reticle-sized ASIC manufactured by TSMC
key_facts.excerpt: The company plans to deploy Jalapeño by the end of this year, and it is the first step in a multi-generation chip development plan... It took the company's engineers roughly nine months to complete the chip design before it sent it to Taiwan's TSMC for manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Early testing shows the first-generation accelerator will deliver performance per watt substantially better than current state-of-the-art; OpenAI says it has run its GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark model on the chip in a test environment
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says it has already begun running at least one of its prior generation models, GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark, on the chips at a workload, though in a test environment.

key_facts.fact: The partnership was originally announced in October 2025; the companies ultimately aim to deploy enough OpenAI-designed chips to require 10 gigawatts of power
key_facts.excerpt: In October, after 18 months spent working together, OpenAI and Broadcom went public with plans to develop and deploy racks of OpenAI-designed chips starting late this year, ultimately aiming to build enough to require 10 gigawatts of power.

stories.headline: Micron posts record $41.5B quarter on AI memory demand, guides Q4 to $50B

key_facts.fact: Micron reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $41.46 billion, up 346% from $9.30 billion a year earlier and above the ~$35.84 billion consensus estimate
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue of $41.46 billion versus $23.86 billion for the prior quarter and $9.30 billion for the same period last year

key_facts.fact: GAAP net income was $28.24 billion ($24.67 per diluted share); non-GAAP EPS of $25.11 beat the ~$20.78 estimate, with adjusted gross margin of 84.9%
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue: $41.46 billion versus $35.84 billion estimated. EPS: $25.11, adjusted, versus $20.78 estimated.

key_facts.fact: Micron guided fiscal Q4 revenue to about $50 billion (range $49-$51 billion), well above the ~$43.58 billion analyst forecast, with gross margin guided to about 86%
key_facts.excerpt: For the current quarter, the company said it expects revenue of about $50 billion, up from $11.3 billion a year earlier. Analysts were looking for a revenue forecast of $43.58 billion.

key_facts.fact: Core data center revenue climbed more than sevenfold to $11.5 billion from $1.53 billion a year ago; cloud memory rose over 300% to $13.77 billion
key_facts.excerpt: the most explosive growth was in the core data center business, where sales climbed more than sevenfold to $11.5 billion from $1.53 billion in the same period a year ago... Cloud memory was up over 300% to $13.77 billion.

key_facts.fact: Micron disclosed 16 strategic customer agreements carrying a minimum of approximately $100 billion in contracted revenue; the stock rose about 15% in extended trading
key_facts.excerpt: announcing 16 multi-year supply agreements that carry a minimum of approximately $100 billion in contracted revenue

stories.headline: IBM debuts world's first sub-1nm chip technology with 3D 'nanostack' transistors

key_facts.fact: IBM on June 25 unveiled the world's first sub-1 nanometer chip technology, a transistor architecture at the 0.7 nm (7 angstrom) node, claiming the first chip technology to operate below the 1 nm threshold
key_facts.excerpt: IBM today unveiled a major semiconductor breakthrough with the introduction of the world's first sub-1 nanometer (nm) chip technology, featuring a revolutionary transistor architecture at the 0.7 nm, or 7 angstrom node.

key_facts.fact: The chip packs nearly 100 billion transistors onto a fingernail-sized chip, roughly twice the density of IBM's 2 nm chip unveiled in 2021, using a 3D 'nanostack' architecture that vertically stacks and staggers transistors
key_facts.excerpt: IBM's new sub-1 nm chip packs nearly 100 billion transistors onto a chip the size of a fingernail, nearly twice the density of IBM's 2 nm chip, unveiled in 2021... The nanostack design vertically stacks and staggers transistors, taking advantage of 3D sequential integration.

key_facts.fact: IBM projects the technology delivers up to 50% more performance or 70% greater energy efficiency versus its 2 nm node, and says its roadmap projects at least a decade of future scaling
key_facts.excerpt: the chip is projected to deliver up to 50% more performance or 70% greater energy efficiency compared to IBM's 2 nm node chips... IBM said its semiconductor roadmap projects at least a decade of future scaling from the new architecture.

key_facts.fact: IBM said it sees a path to production of the nanostack technology within approximately five years
key_facts.excerpt: IBM indicated it sees a path to production of nanostack technology within approximately five years.

stories.headline: Intel-backed AI chip firm SambaNova set to raise up to $1B at a $10B valuation

key_facts.fact: SambaNova is looking to raise up to $1 billion at a post-money valuation of $10 billion, roughly five times its valuation of just four months ago, executive chairman and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said
key_facts.excerpt: SambaNova Systems, the Palo Alto-based AI chip maker, is looking to raise up to $1 billion at a post-money valuation of $10 billion. That figure is roughly five times what the company was valued at just four months ago.

key_facts.fact: The startup could raise between $800 million and $1 billion in the new round, amid rising demand for cheaper AI inference chips
key_facts.excerpt: AI chipmaker SambaNova could raise between US$800 million and US$1 billion in a new funding round, according to its executive chairman and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan. This would raise SambaNova's value to US$10 billion.

key_facts.fact: The target valuation is up from a roughly $2.2-$4.8 billion range implied by SambaNova's $350 million Series E in February 2026, led by Vista Equity Partners and Cambium Capital with Intel Capital participating
key_facts.excerpt: SambaNova closed its Series E round in February 2026, raising approximately $350 million. That round, led by Vista Equity Partners and Cambium Capital with Intel participating, implied a valuation somewhere between $2.2 billion and $4.8 billion.

key_facts.fact: A $10 billion valuation would nearly double SambaNova's prior all-time high of $5.1 billion set after its 2021 Series D led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2
key_facts.excerpt: It would also nearly double its previous all-time high valuation of $5.1 billion, which came after a $676 million Series D round in 2021 led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2.

stories.headline: Kioxia plans US depositary share listing in spring 2027 amid AI memory boom

key_facts.fact: Kioxia Holdings, Japan's most valuable company, plans to offer US depositary shares in spring 2027 (targeting April-June) to tap demand for AI-related semiconductor stocks, CFO Yoshihiko Kawamura said at the company's annual shareholders' meeting
key_facts.excerpt: Kioxia Holdings plans to offer U.S. depositary shares in the spring of 2027 and a stock split to take advantage of runaway demand for exposure to AI-related semiconductor stocks.

key_facts.fact: The NAND flash maker is also considering a domestic stock split to broaden its retail investor base, after its shares surpassed ¥100,000 ($620) on Thursday and rose nearly 900% this year
key_facts.excerpt: Kioxia... also said it is actively considering a stock split domestically to expand its investor base. Its shares surpassed ¥100,000 ($620) apiece on Thursday, helped by blowout results from memory maker Micron Technology, and adding to a nearly 900% rise this year.

key_facts.fact: Kioxia shares rose as much as 15% on Thursday, extending this year's gain to nearly 800%, after the listing plan and Micron's strong results lifted semiconductor stocks across Asia
key_facts.excerpt: Kioxia's shares rose as much as 15% on Thursday, extending gains to nearly 800% this year, after the company said it aims to tap the U.S. market shortly after the end of its current fiscal year in March 2027.

key_facts.fact: The move follows SK Hynix's US listing plan announced a day earlier; both Japanese and Korean memory makers are seeking access to US capital markets
key_facts.excerpt: Kioxia joins South Korea's SK Hynix, which announced plans for a U.S. listing on Wednesday, while stronger-than-expected quarterly results from Micron Technology helped lift semiconductor stocks across Asia.

stories.headline: Netherlands lobbies US to drop MATCH Act chip curbs that would hit ASML's China sales

key_facts.fact: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma met US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and lawmakers in Washington to press against the MATCH Act, which would bar Chinese chipmakers from accessing chipmaking equipment
key_facts.excerpt: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma on June 23 met with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and lawmakers in Washington, where Congress has been debating the so-called MATCH Act, which would bar Chinese chipmakers from accessing the equipment.

key_facts.fact: The most significant expansion in the US bill would curb all of ASML's deep ultraviolet immersion (immersion DUV) machines, building on existing EUV controls; ASML is Europe's most valuable company
key_facts.excerpt: Among the most significant expansions in the US bill would be curbs on all of ASML's deep ultraviolet immersion lithography, or immersion DUV, machines. That would build on existing controls of the most-advanced extreme ultraviolet lithography, or EUV, machines.

key_facts.fact: China accounted for 19% of ASML's net system sales in Q1, down from 36% in the previous quarter; the Dutch government opposes the bill, criticizing its extraterritorial character
key_facts.excerpt: China... accounted for 19 per cent of net system sales in the first quarter, down from 36 per cent in the previous quarter... The Dutch government opposes the bill, criticising its extraterritorial character as it is imposing restrictions on another country's sovereign trade policies.

key_facts.fact: Sjoerdsma said the visit was 'exceptional' and would be followed by further meetings to press US officials to reconsider; the bipartisan MATCH Act was proposed in April
key_facts.excerpt: The Match Act, a bipartisan bill proposed in April, would make it harder for Chinese chipmakers to produce AI semiconductors, in part by setting up mechanisms to coerce allied countries to keep more equipment from China.
